cues.en: Nope. Didn't think so. Anyway, so off into the countryside.
cues.zh: 不能。我觉得不行。总之，那就出发去乡下吧。

cues.en: Where I discovered these brilliant multi colored layered mountains. You know as a child you get the sets where you get sand of different colors and pour it on top of yourself.
cues.zh: 我在那儿发现了这些绚丽的、色彩斑斓的层状山脉。你知道，小时候你买过那种装有不同颜色沙子的套装，然后往自己身上倒。

cues.en: I think that's where they got the idea from is from here. You can see all the different colors and also here's a here's a how to on how I get some of the best available camera shots by offloading.
cues.zh: 我想他们的灵感就是从这儿来的。你可以看到所有这些不同的颜色，还有，这里有个教程，教我如何通过卸载来拍到一些现成的最佳镜头。

cues.en: Come on, little 90.
cues.zh: 加油，小90。

cues.en: Yes.
cues.zh: 太棒了。

cues.en: The colors also got more vivid the further north you went.
cues.zh: 越往北走，颜色也越发鲜艳。

cues.en: Remember, I'm in Iran, so you're never too far away from free food or drink.
cues.zh: 记住，我在伊朗，所以你离免费的吃喝永远不会太远。

cues.en: So I was just taking some pictures of these cool tractors. The guys invited me in for some tea.
cues.zh: 我当时正在拍这些酷炫的拖拉机，小伙子们邀请我进去喝茶。

cues.en: So cool. Now I did meet one unfriendly person in Iran. He was a Polish guy riding a BMW GS. I pulled alongside and waved to him, you know, because we're both traveling. He just looked down on me and sped off. So that's why I decided to get my own back. Eventually, I caught him up in traffic.
cues.zh: 太酷了。不过我在伊朗确实遇到过一个不友好的人。他是个骑着宝马 GS 的波兰人。我把车开到他旁边跟他挥手，你知道的，因为我们都在旅行。他却对我满脸不屑，然后加速跑了。所以我决定报复他。最终，我在车流中追上了他。

cues.en: And every time there was a small gap, I could filter through it, he couldn't. So I did this over and over looking more and more smug until eventually I whipped out the camera and then he turned off.
cues.zh: 每当有一小条缝隙，我都能钻过去，而他不行。于是我一次又一次地这么做，表情越来越得意，直到最后我掏出相机，他就拐弯溜了。

cues.en: The GS owner won't talk to me. Oh, well.
cues.zh: GS 车主不理我。好吧。

cues.en: Time to show him how to filter.
cues.zh: 是时候教教他怎么在车流中穿行了。

cues.en: During this update, you might have seen these screens that Iranians fit to their motorcycles, and I think they look crap and really uncool.
cues.zh: 在这个更新里，你可能见过伊朗人装在摩托车上的这种挡风屏，我觉得它们看起来丑透了，一点都不酷。

cues.en: So I bought one, and it cost me £3,
cues.zh: 所以我买了一个，花了我3英镑，

cues.en: and the window in the middle is actually glass.
cues.zh: 中间的窗户居然是玻璃的。

cues.en: But it was my last full day in Iran. But before I left, this cool guy called Behzad, is on the right here, and his daughter, Otina, and his brother-in-law,
cues.zh: 但那是我在伊朗的最后一个完整日子。临走之前，有个叫Behzad的酷小伙——右边这位——还有他女儿Otina和他姐夫，

cues.en: I think, on the left, took me out to this Iranian theme park, which was really cool. It's my final night. Here's Otina. She's always running around causing mischief.
cues.zh: 应该是左边这位，带我去了这个伊朗主题公园，真的很酷。那是我最后一晚。这是Otina，她总是到处跑来跑去捣乱。

cues.en: Also, to any parents who want to silence their children, these are a brilliant idea. Airtight balls that you just get a child, put them in it, chuck them on the water, and they're absolutely helpless to try and get themselves free.
cues.zh: 另外，对任何想让孩子安静下来的父母来说，这玩意儿简直是绝妙主意。密封的充气球，你把孩子放进去，往水面上一扔，他们完全没法自己挣脱出来。

cues.en: This is also window shopping my style. There you can get all your components for your c 90. There's clutches, carburettors,
cues.zh: 这也是我风格的橱窗购物。在那儿你能买到C90的所有零件。有离合器、化油器、

cues.en: crankshafts, the lot.
cues.zh: 曲轴，应有尽有。

cues.en: But we are still in Iran, so it is free food time again.
cues.zh: 但我们还在伊朗，所以又到了免费食物时间。

cues.en: Well, I just bought some engine oil from that shop and after
cues.zh: 我刚从那家店买了些机油，然后

cues.en: I paid for it and I was just about to leave, they gave me some cake.
cues.zh: 我付完钱正准备走，他们给了我一些蛋糕。

cues.en: For free food, it's amazing.
cues.zh: 免费食物，太棒了。

cues.en: So that was Iran. This is me on the road to the Turkish border. Iran is my favorite country by far. Everybody there acts like your friend's nan. You know how when you go around there and your mates nan will be like, oh, would you like some cake? Would you like to sit here? Is there anything I can get you? Would you like me to do this? Would you like to change the channel on the TV? You know? Just endlessly, relentlessly friendly.
cues.zh: 这就是伊朗。这是我在前往土耳其边境的路上。伊朗是我目前为止最喜欢的国家。那里每个人都像你朋友的奶奶一样。你知道的，你去那边的时候，你朋友的奶奶会说，哦，要来点蛋糕吗？要坐这儿吗？需要我给你拿点什么吗？要我帮你做这个吗？要我帮你换电视 channel 吗？你知道吧？就是无止境、毫不松懈地友好。

cues.en: And,
cues.zh: 还有，

cues.en: yeah, it's it's bizarre.
cues.zh: 是啊，这……这太离奇了。

cues.en: Even when I was at the police and military checkpoints, they'd ask to see your passport and you'd show it to them and then they'd, like, bring out the tea and the cigarettes and you'd be talking there, you know, like, sometimes for an hour just showing them pictures of your trip. So it isn't as even if it's just the people there. It is everybody down to the police and the army. If I could choose any country in the world to basically, you know, wake up naked in the middle of nowhere with no money and I had to try and find my way back to, you know, civilization and help, it would be Iran.
cues.zh: 就算在警察和军队的检查站，他们也会要看你的护照，你给他们看，然后他们就会拿出茶和烟，你就在那儿聊，有时候能聊一个小时，就给他们看你旅行的照片。所以并不只是那里的普通人这样。连警察和军队都这样。如果让我选世界上任何一个国家，基本上就是，你知道，在荒郊野外赤身醒来、身无分文，还得自己想办法回到文明社会求助，那我会选伊朗。

cues.en: It's just... That's brilliant. And I will go back there in a heartbeat and I know I will again at some point.
cues.zh: 只是……太棒了。我会毫不犹豫再回那里，我知道以后某个时候我还会再去。

cues.en: Yeah. So hopefully you've enjoyed this update. Hopefully, it's given you the side that the papers for some reason don't want you to see. My cynical view would be it so that when America does invade, there's not gonna be that much public opposition to it because everybody by that point would have be conditioned to think that Iran is evil. So maybe that's just me being cynical. So anyway, there you are. That's the Ed March story of Iran. Like I said, nothing scripted. That's it. You know, job done.
cues.zh: 是啊。希望你喜欢这次更新。希望它让你看到了报纸不知为何不想让你看到的那一面。我愤世嫉俗的看法是，这样等美国真的入侵时，公众就不会那么反对了，因为到那时所有人都已经被灌输得认为伊朗是邪恶的。也许这只是我太愤世嫉俗了。总之，就是这样。这就是 Ed March 的伊朗故事。就像我说的，没有剧本。就这样。你知道，搞定。
